title: Hamas-led attack on southern Israel from Gaza
body:
On 7 October 2023, during the Jewish holiday of Simchat Torah, Hamas-led militants launched a surprise attack from the Gaza Strip into southern Israel. The assault, which Hamas named Operation Al-Aqsa Flood, began with a barrage of rockets and was followed by fighters crossing the border fence by land, sea and air. Attackers struck about 21 communities in the Gaza envelope, including Be'eri, Kfar Aza, Nir Oz and Netiv HaAsara, as well as military bases.

According to Israeli figures, 1,195 people were killed, among them at least 828 civilians and 367 members of the security forces. Israel also reported that about 1,200 attackers were killed. At the Nova music festival near Re'im, 364 civilians were killed, according to the same Israeli accounts. Israeli authorities reported that 251 Israeli and foreign civilians and soldiers were taken as hostages into the Gaza Strip.

Israel responded by declaring a state of war and launching a large-scale military operation in Gaza. Later in the conflict, the Hamas-run Gaza Health Ministry began publishing its own casualty figures for Palestinians killed in Israeli operations, which Israel and others have disputed in various ways. The events of 7 October became the starting point of the Gaza war, which drew in regional actors including Hezbollah, the Houthis and Iran.
